## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has integral Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\), with \(q=n-r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- [source-backed] The antipode satisfies \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\); the resulting integral Hopf identity is proved there. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]
- [proved] Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), and assume \(a+j\le r,\ a+i\le q,\ b\le i,j\). For every \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
  \[
  [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
  =(-1)^{|\rho|}
  [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]
  \quad\text{in }Q. \tag{E}
  \]
- [computed] For \((i,j,a,b)=(2,3,2,2)\), (E) gives
  \[
  [222]=[222],\quad [2221]=-[322],\quad [2222]=[332],
  \]
  \[
  [22211]=[422],\quad [22221]=-[432],\quad [22222]=[442],
  \]
  against complete integral relation lattices. [artifact b525c6b69aec42dfda85ba9b819a6a11265e17552b8c81c742e5f276ef669fc4]

## Strategy
Write \(\rho=(\rho _1,\ldots,\rho_a)\), padded by zeros, and
\[
\rho'_k=\#\{\ell: \rho_\ell\ge k\}\qquad(1\le k\le b),
\]
also padded by zeros. Thus
\[
L_\rho=(i^j,\rho),\qquad
R_\rho=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})
\]
are partitions: \(\rho_1\le b\le i\), \(\rho'_1\le a\), \(b\le j\), and the parameter inequalities put both in \(q^r\).

The full-coordinate Hopf descent, equivalently the antipode/Cauchy–Binet expansion with
\(S(s_\mu)=(-1)^{|\mu|}s_{\mu'}\), gives the integral rectangular-straightening identity
\[
s_{L_\rho}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho}
 =\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}F_{\rho,\sigma}s_{L_\sigma},
\qquad
F_{\rho,\sigma}\in\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}. \tag{1}
\]
Here every coefficient has strictly positive degree. This is the full-coordinate form: no \(\theta\)-coordinates are discarded. It follows by expanding the Hopf identity in the Schur basis; the two endpoint terms are \(L_\rho\) and \(R_\rho\), and every other term has lower attachment \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\). The endpoint sign is exactly the antipode sign \((-1)^{|\rho|}\).

After projection to \(A\), each \(\bar s_{L_\sigma}\) lies in \(J_v\), while
\(\bar F_{\rho,\sigma}\in A_+\). Hence every summand on the right of (1) lies in \(A_+J_v\). Passing to \(Q\) proves (E). The accepted graded-kernel presentation ensures that these are equalities in the integral quotient \(Q\), with no torsion or unrecorded kernel ambiguity.

Boundary cases: if \(\rho=\varnothing\), then \(L_\rho=R_\rho=i^j\), so (E) is the identity. If \(a=0\), this is the only \(\rho\). Zero parts in \(\rho\) and \(\rho'\) are omitted from displayed partitions.

## Gaps
No gap remains for this signed-conjugation certificate, conditional on the accepted full-coordinate Hopf descent and graded-kernel presentation. This certificate alone does not assert the parent theorem.
